cultural_notes: over 15,000 Basques settled the Treasure Valley, making it the largest community of Basques outside Europe; the Basque Block on Grove Street is a walkable district of a museum, market, restaurants and boardinghouse history (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasure_Valley; visitsouthwestidaho.org Basque Block; visitboise.com Basque)

the Cyrus Jacobs-Uberuaga House on the Basque Block is the oldest surviving brick building in Boise (1864); Jaialdi, a major Basque festival, fills the block (source: visitboise.com Basque; visitsouthwestidaho.org Jaialdi)
Basques came in the mid-1800s and became indispensable sheepherders in Idaho's rugged high country -- a deep agricultural-heritage story (source: nationalgeographic.com Basque culture in Idaho)
the Boise Foothills and Bogus Basin (16 mi from downtown) give the metro an accessible ski-and-trail outdoor identity (source: bogusbasin.org; visitsouthwestidaho.org)
